name: Nazca culture
title: The story of the Nazca culture

text: About 2,100 years ago, the Nazca people lived in river valleys in the desert of southern Peru.
They wove cloth of cotton and wool, and the dry desert has kept much of it safe in their graves.
src: The Nazca lived in the river valleys of Peru’s southern desert from about 100 BCE to 800 CE
Nazca textiles, woven probably by women on backstrap looms from cotton and wool / burials, whose textiles have been preserved by the dry desert

text: They were farmers who grew maize, beans, squash, sweet potatoes and peanuts.
Llamas carried their loads and gave them wool and meat.
src: The Nazca lived mainly by farming. They ate maize, squash, beans, sweet potato, manioc, achira and peanuts
Llamas carried loads and gave wool and meat

text: To water their fields, they dug channels under the ground, called puquios, down to the water below.
Several dozen puquios still carry water today.
src: they built puquios to farm the desert: underground channels dug into hillsides until they reached the water table
Several dozen puquios still carry water today

text: At Cahuachi, a holy place, they held ceremonies for spirits that were part human, part animal, to help crops grow.
Ritual leaders seem to have used the San Pedro cactus, and heads of the dead were used in ceremonies.
src: Their art shows powerful nature spirits as mythical beings that mix human, animal, bird and fish features / Ceremonies took place at Cahuachi, where people worshipped these beings to help their crops grow
Shamans apparently used the San Pedro cactus / Severed human heads, called trophy heads, were used in rituals

text: About 1,500 years ago, their way of life began to fail.
Great floods probably washed the soil away, made worse because many trees had been cut down.
src: From about 500 CE Nazca society declined
A likely cause is an El Niño that brought widespread, destructive floods. / The Nazca may have made these worse by gradually cutting down Prosopis pallida trees / eroding the soil

text: They made the Nazca Lines, huge animal shapes and long lines in the desert, by moving its red stones aside.
No one knows for sure why, but the lines remain, along with pots painted in many colours.
src: The Nazca Lines are geometric shapes, long lines and huge animal figures / who removed the red surface pebbles to expose the lighter ground
no theory has been proved / The dry desert has preserved the Nazca Lines for centuries / Nazca pottery is painted in at least twelve colours
